extracted.intended_audience: children's book illustrators, librarians, authors, and general readers interested in the Caldecott Medal
extracted.subtask_description: Describes eligibility, evaluation criteria, and selection procedures for the Caldecott Medal — the annual ALA award for the most distinguished American picture book illustrations — along with historical context and notable winners.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distinguished illustrations / excellence of pictorial presentation
rubrics_metrics.description: The Caldecott Medal is for 'distinguished illustrations in a picture book' and for 'excellence of pictorial presentation for children.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is the core evaluative standard for the award — the committee seeks outstanding pictorial work in picture books intended for children. Examples of past winners (e.g., Where the Wild Things Are, This Is Not My Hat) illustrate the level of distinction expected.

rubrics_metrics.name: Award recipient (to whom the medal is given)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Caldecott Medal is given to the book's illustrator by the Association for Library Service to Children (ALSC), a division of the American Library Association (ALA).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The recognition is explicitly for the illustrator (not the author), and any distinctions (Medal vs. Honors) are decided by the committee.

rubrics_metrics.name: Illustrator eligibility (citizenship/residency)
rubrics_metrics.description: To be considered for the Caldecott Award, an illustrator must be a United States citizen or resident.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This eligibility requirement restricts the pool to illustrators with U.S. citizenship or residency status.

rubrics_metrics.name: Originality of illustrations
rubrics_metrics.description: The illustrations must be original for the picture book.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Illustrations previously published elsewhere or not created specifically for the eligible picture book would fail this requirement; original pictorial content created for the book is required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication timing and language
rubrics_metrics.description: The picture book must have been published in the U.S. in English during the previous year to be considered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Eligibility is tied to U.S. publication in English and limited to books published in the calendar year prior to the award year.

rubrics_metrics.name: Intended audience age limit
rubrics_metrics.description: Books must be intended for audiences up to age 14 in order to be considered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The award targets picture books for children and youth; books intended primarily for older audiences would be ineligible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selection committee composition
rubrics_metrics.description: A Caldecott Selection committee comprised of 15 members decides on the Caldecott Award winner each year. Eight committee members are selected by the ALSC and seven, including the chairperson, are appointed by the ALSC President.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This specifies the committee size and appointment process, which shapes how deliberations and decisions are made.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nomination and review process
rubrics_metrics.description: Publishers commonly send copies of picture books to the committee for review, but committee members are also asked by the chairperson to identify strong candidates. Each committee member must nominate books throughout the year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Eligibility depends not only on meeting formal criteria but also on being brought to the committee's attention via publisher submissions and active member nominations across the year.

rubrics_metrics.name: Caldecott Honors for runners-up
rubrics_metrics.description: In addition to books that win the distinguished Caldecott Medal, the committee has awarded Honors to various runners-up each year since 1971.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The committee may designate one or more Honor books in recognition of outstanding pictorial work that did not receive the Medal; this practice broadens formal recognition beyond a single winner.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope/timing of the award (annual, for previous year's books)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Caldecott Medal annually recognizes the previous year's most distinguished American picture book for children.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The award is given once per year and is retrospective, assessing books published in the prior year.
